chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali narrated to me from his father from Ali ibn Muhammad from Abdullah ibn Muqatil from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever has faith in Allah and the Last Day, let him apply antimony (kohl).

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the Accepting One), a title of the eighth Imam
key_terms.يَكْتَحِلْ: Let him apply kohl/antimony (iktihal), a specific ritual action

ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of applying antimony (kohl) in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-Amal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Rida (AS) linking the physical act of applying antimony (kohl) to spiritual faith in God and the Hereafter, elevating it from mere hygiene to a recommended sunnah. This hadith reflects the Shia tradition of integrating bodily care with devotional practice, suggesting that maintaining one's appearance and health is an expression of gratitude and readiness for the afterlife.
